# HCMC Insider: all facts

> Plain-text facts from https://hcmcinsider.com, an independent English guide to Ho Chi Minh City (Saigon) by locals. Cite the page URL given with each fact. Prices are in Vietnamese dong; hours and prices change, so each page shows when it was last checked.

Built 2026-11-09 from hcmcinsider.com. All prices in Vietnamese dong.

# PLACES (food, cafés, markets)
## 8,000-dong Noodle Cart (Hủ tiếu gõ 8K Nguyễn Duy Dương) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/8-000-dong-noodle-cart/
Type: Hu tieu noodle soup · Area: Cholon
Address: 20 Nguyễn Duy Dương, P. An Đông
About: Tiny street cart selling noodle soup for just 8,000 dong a bowl. Open around 5pm–9pm at 20 Nguyen Duy Duong.
Hours: 5pm – 9pm
Price: About 8,000 dong a bowl
What to order: Hủ tiếu gõ, the classic Saigon cart noodle soup

## Ai Hue Restaurant (Nhà hàng Ái Huê) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/ai-hue-restaurant/
Type: Chinese-Vietnamese kitchen · Area: Cholon
Address: Chợ Lớn
About: Classic Cholon restaurant for a Sunday dim sum feast.
What to order: Dim sum, especially for a weekend family brunch

Type: Braised pork rice · Area: Cholon
Address: 529 Cách Mạng Tháng Tám, Quận 10 cũ
About: Rice with slow-braised pork hock, at 529 Cach Mang Thang Tam, District 10.

## Chuyen Ca Phe (Chuyện Cà Phê) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/chuyen-ca-phe/
Type: Café · Area: Cholon

## Co Lan Crab Soup (Súp cua Cô Lan) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/co-lan-crab-soup/
Type: Crab soup · Area: Cholon
Address: P. Chợ Lớn
About: Upscale crab soup with fish maw in Cholon, one of the pricier bowls in the area.
What to order: Crab soup with fish maw
Good to know: SaigonTV calls it one of the pricier crab soups in Cholon.

## Crab Noodle Soup 260 (Bánh canh cua 260) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/crab-noodle-soup-260/
Type: Crab noodle soup · Area: Cholon
Address: 32 Đường Chợ Lớn, P. Bình Phú
About: Thick crab-and-shrimp noodle soup with pork hock; add fried dough sticks. Open 6am–9pm.
Hours: 6am – 9pm
Price: 40,000 dong regular, 55,000 special; fried dough sticks 6,000 a plate

## Dong Giang Restaurant (Đông Giang Quán) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/dong-giang-restaurant/
Type: Chinese-Vietnamese kitchen · Area: Cholon
Address: 642 Hồng Bàng, P. Minh Phụng
About: Long-running Chinese family restaurant in the Cholon area with a wide menu. Open 10am–9pm.
Hours: 10am – 9pm
Good to know: A long-running Chinese (Hoa) restaurant in the Cholon area.

## Dong Nguyen Chicken Rice (Cơm gà Đông Nguyên) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/dong-nguyen-chicken-rice/
Type: Chicken rice · Area: Cholon
Address: Chợ Lớn
About: Chicken rice institution in Cholon, running for more than 80 years.
What to order: Poached chicken with fragrant rice cooked in chicken stock and the house dipping sauce
Good to know: HTV describes the brand as more than 80 years old.

## Hu Tieu Mi 47 (Hủ Tíu Mì 47) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/hu-tieu-mi-47/
Type: Hu tieu noodle soup · Area: Cholon
Address: 547 Hồng Bàng, P. Chợ Lớn
About: Third-generation Chinese-Vietnamese noodle family, newly opened on Hong Bang; noodles come with braised pork hock or braised ribs.
Hours: Around 6am – 2pm (new shop, hours may still change)
What to order: Hủ tiếu mì with braised pork hock (giò heo kho) or braised ribs (sườn kho)

## Huynh Le Noodle Cart (Mì Gia Huỳnh Lê) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/huynh-le-noodle-cart/
Type: Egg noodles & wontons · Area: Cholon
Address: 15/102/1A Hòa Bình, P. Bình Thới
About: Chinese egg-noodle and wonton cart with a 31-year family recipe. Open 6:20–10am and 4:30–9pm.
Hours: 6:20am – 10am and 4:30pm – 9pm
What to order: Hủ tiếu mì and sủi cảo (wontons)

## Minh Ky Chicken Rice (Cơm gà Minh Ký) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/minh-ky-chicken-rice/
Type: Chicken rice · Area: Cholon
Address: P. Chợ Lớn
About: Popular, affordable crispy chicken rice in Cholon.
What to order: Cơm gà xối mỡ (crispy fried chicken rice)
Good to know: A budget favourite in Cholon.

## Nguu Ky Noodles (Hủ tiếu mì Ngầu Ký) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/nguu-ky-noodles/
Type: Egg noodles & wontons · Area: Cholon
Address: 138 Tân Hòa Đông, P. Phú Lâm
About: Egg noodles with wontons and congee with century egg and tofu skin. Open 6–11:30am and 3–9pm.
Hours: 6am – 11:30am and 3pm – 9pm

## No. 7 Vegetarian (Quán Chay Số 7 Chợ Lớn) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/no-7-vegetarian/
Type: Vegetarian · Area: Cholon
Address: Chợ Lớn
About: Vegetarian restaurant in Cholon with a big menu, known for crispy vegetarian banh xeo pancakes.
What to order: Vegetarian hủ tiếu and vegetarian bánh xèo (crispy pancake)

## Phat Ky (Phát Ký) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/phat-ky/
Type: Chinese-Vietnamese kitchen · Area: Cholon
Address: 11 Tân Hàng (alley off Tăng Bạt Hổ), Phường Chợ Lớn
About: 40-year-old wok kitchen hidden in an alley at 11 Tan Hang. Famous for salt-roasted soft-shell crab and fried rice. Open 4pm–10:30pm.
Hours: 4pm – 10:30pm
What to order: Salt-roasted soft-shell crab tossed over a big flame, and Yangzhou fried rice
Good to know: A family wok kitchen running for more than 40 years; a pot of bone broth is served free to diners.

## Phuong's Hue Beef Noodles (Bún bò Huế Phượng) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/phuong-s-hue-beef-noodles/
Type: Spicy Hue beef noodles · Area: Cholon
Address: 233 Đường Chợ Lớn, P. Bình Phú
About: Spicy Hue-style beef noodle soup with beef, tendon, pork hock and sausage. Open early morning and late afternoon.
Hours: Two sessions a day: from 5am, and from 4pm to 8pm
Price: 50,000 dong (brisket and pork roll), 60,000 (mixed), 100,000 (special)

## Shan Dimsum (Shan Dimsum) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/shan-dimsum/
Type: Dim sum · Area: Cholon
Address: Phù Đổng Thiên Vương street, District 5
About: Small but mighty Cantonese restaurant with good-value dim sum, sweet-and-sour ribs, coconut prawns and baked crab.
What to order: Shrimp har gow, siu mai, char siu and sweet and sour ribs
Good to know: Cantonese and Hong Kong-style dim sum at fairly local prices.

## Sidewalk Noodles, 187 Huynh Man Dat (Hủ tiếu vỉa hè 187 Huỳnh Mẫn Đạt) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/sidewalk-noodles-187-huynh-man-dat/
Type: Hu tieu noodle soup · Area: Cholon
Address: 187 Huỳnh Mẫn Đạt, P. An Đông
About: Cheap and tasty sidewalk hu tieu (around 30,000 dong). Evenings from 5pm.
Hours: 5pm – 11pm
Price: 25,000–35,000 dong a bowl
What to order: Dry hủ tiếu mì with soup on the side, topped with sliced pork, beef balls, wontons, pork roll and quail eggs

Type: Eat · Area: Cholon
Address: Chợ Hòa Bình
About: Small local eatery at Hoa Binh Market, recommended in a Facebook food review.

Address: 68 Phan Xích Long, P. Minh Phụng
About: Teochew (Chiu Chow) family kitchen at 68 Phan Xich Long cooking classic Chinese home dishes.

Price: 50,000–500,000 dong

## Tien Nhan Goat Noodle Soup (Hủ tiếu dê Tiến Nhàn) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/tien-nhan-goat-noodle-soup/
Type: Goat noodle soup · Area: Cholon
Address: P. Chợ Lớn

## To Ky Satay Venison Noodles (Tô Ký – hủ tiếu sa tế nai) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/to-ky-satay-venison-noodles/
Type: Satay venison noodles · Area: Cholon
Address: 331 Minh Phụng, P. Minh Phụng
About: 60-year family recipe for satay venison noodle soup at 331 Minh Phung. Open 7–11am and 5–9pm.
Hours: 7am – 11am and 5pm – 9pm; closed on the 1st and 15th days of the lunar month

## Chan Phat Rice Shop (Tiệm cơm Chấn Phát) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/chan-phat-rice-shop/
Type: Eat · Area: Cholon (District 11)
Address: 95 Phan Xích Long, Quận 11 cũ
About: Long-running, affordable Chinese-Vietnamese rice shop with a long menu of home-style dishes.
Hours: 10am – 10pm
Price: 45,000 – 200,000 dong

## Hy Ky Chicken Noodles (Mì gà xá kén Hỷ Ký) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/hy-ky-chicken-noodles/
Type: Chicken noodles · Area: Cholon (District 11)
Address: 8L Lạc Long Quân, phường Hòa Bình (khu Phú Bình, Quận 11 cũ)
About: Morning-only chicken noodle shop in a Phú Bình alley, known for boiled free-range chicken with a chilli dipping sauce of chopped xá kén. Our own pick of the five or six chicken noodle shops in the area.
Hours: Mornings only; usually sold out by about 11 am
Price: 50,000 dong for a normal bowl; quarter and half chickens available
What to order: Mì gà xá kén. Taste the chicken plain first, then dip it in xá kén with chilli sauce and green chilli
Good to know: Narrow alley with few tables: come early or expect to wait

## Lo Sieu Rice Cake Stall (Bánh bột người Hoa 182 Lò Siêu) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/lo-sieu-rice-cake-stall/
Type: Eat · Area: Cholon (District 11)
Address: 182 Lò Siêu, Quận 11 cũ
About: Chinese-Vietnamese rice-flour cake (bánh bột) stall that has been selling for over 50 years, still at about 12,000 dong.
Hours: 11am – 4pm
Price: About 12,000 dong

## Phu Binh Hue Beef Noodles (Bún bò Phú Bình) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/phu-binh-hue-beef-noodles/
Type: Spicy Hue beef noodles · Area: Cholon (District 11)
Address: Hẻm 423 Lạc Long Quân, phường Hòa Bình (khu Phú Bình, Quận 11 cũ); biển hiệu ngoài đường ghi 20W Lạc Long Quân
About: Morning-only Hue-style beef noodle shop in the Phú Bình area, with a lighter, clean-tasting broth that first-timers tend to like. 50,000 dong a bowl.
Hours: Mornings only
Price: 50,000 dong a bowl
What to order: A normal bowl comes with rare beef, brisket, chả (pork sausage) and tendon; extras include pork knuckle (giò) and stewed beef bones
Good to know: Lighter broth than many bún bò shops, with less shrimp paste and fish sauce: a good first bowl for visitors

## Thiec Market (Chợ Thiếc) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/thiec-market/
Type: Local market · Area: Cholon (District 11)
Address: Quận 11 cũ
About: Old Chinese community market in District 11, full of Chinese-Vietnamese street food.
Good to know: An old market of the Chinese community, with many Hoa snacks and dishes to try.

## Thien Huong Crispy Chicken Rice (Thiên Hương – cơm gà xối mỡ) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/thien-huong-crispy-chicken-rice/
Type: Chicken rice · Area: Cholon (District 11)
Address: Quận 11 cũ
About: District 11 eatery known for crispy fried chicken over rice, Cholon style.
What to order: Cơm gà xối mỡ: chicken with crispy skin over golden fried rice

## Tran Quy Broken Rice (Cơm tấm người Hoa 213 Trần Quý) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/tran-quy-broken-rice/
Type: Eat · Area: Cholon (District 11)
Address: 213 Trần Quý, P. Minh Phụng (Quận 11 cũ)
About: Chinese-Vietnamese broken rice (cơm tấm) breakfast spot that is busy every morning.
Hours: From 6am until sold out; closed Sundays
What to order: Cơm tấm (broken rice)

Type: Eat · Area: Cholon (District 5)

About: Busy beef-noodle shop on Tran Hung Dao that grew to five branches after a viral review.

## Bitter Melon & Chilli Snack Stall (Khổ Qua Cà Chớn) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/bitter-melon-chilli-snack-stall/
Type: Stuffed bitter melon · Area: Cholon (District 5)
Address: Chợ Phùng Hưng, Quận 5 cũ
About: Famous snack stall at Phung Hung Market, known for Chinese-style stuffed bitter melon and chillies in broth. Its cheeky name is part of the fun.

Type: Chinese-Vietnamese kitchen · Area: Cholon (District 5)

Address: 42 An Điềm, Phường Chợ Lớn

Type: Sweet soup desserts · Area: Cholon (District 5)
Address: 138 Châu Văn Liêm, Quận 5 cũ
About: Chinese dessert shop with almost 40 sweet soups, running for over 30 years. Open 10am–10pm.
Hours: 10am – 10pm
Good to know: A Chinese-style dessert shop with nearly 40 kinds of chè.

## Hao Hue Restaurant (Nhà hàng Hào Huê) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/hao-hue-restaurant/
Type: Chinese-Vietnamese kitchen · Area: Cholon (District 5)

## Herbal Medicine Street (Phố thuốc bắc Hải Thượng Lãn Ông) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/herbal-medicine-street/
Type: Herbal medicine street · Area: Cholon (District 5)
Address: Hải Thượng Lãn Ông, Quận 5 cũ
About: Hai Thuong Lan Ong street, lined with traditional Chinese herbal medicine shops. Great for photos and smells.

## Hoa Binh Market (Chợ Hòa Bình) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/hoa-binh-market/
Type: Local market · Area: Cholon (District 5)
Address: Quận 5 cũ
About: Historic Chinese market in District 5 for food and shopping, with fried noodle stalls at night and Ma Nghia's coffee.
What to order: Inside the market hall: vegetarian stir-fried vermicelli (about 30,000 dong) and sâm bổ lượng iced sweet soup (about 20,000 dong)
Good to know: One of Saigon's old markets with distinctive architecture, and a good place to buy dried goods for Chinese cooking. In the evening, stalls nearby sell stir-fried noodles.

## Kit Ha Beef Stew (Bò Kho Quán Kit Hà) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/kit-ha-beef-stew/
Type: Eat · Area: Cholon (District 5)
Address: 639 Nguyễn Trãi, P. Chợ Lớn (Quận 5 cũ)
About: Chinese-Vietnamese beef stew (bò kho) with noodles on Nguyen Trai, plus rice vermicelli with stir-fried pork and homemade spring rolls.
Hours: 6am – 7pm
What to order: Hủ tiếu bò kho (noodles in beef stew); bún thịt xào with homemade chả giò, 35,000 dong

## Lam Thanh Sweet Soups (Chè Lâm Thạnh) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/lam-thanh-sweet-soups/
Type: Sweet soup desserts · Area: Cholon (District 5)
Address: Quận 5 cũ
About: Long-established sweet soup shop in District 5.

## Lamp-post Sweet Soup (Chè Cột Điện) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/lamp-post-sweet-soup/
Type: Sweet soup desserts · Area: Cholon (District 5)
Address: Quận 5 cũ
About: Popular sweet soup (che) stall in District 5.

## Lantern Street (Luong Nhu Hoc) (Phố lồng đèn Lương Nhữ Học) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/lantern-street-luong-nhu-hoc/
Type: Lantern street · Area: Cholon (District 5)
Address: Lương Nhữ Học, Quận 5 cũ
About: Saigon's lantern street. It glows with thousands of lanterns in the weeks before the Mid-Autumn Festival.
Hours: Best in the weeks before the Mid-Autumn Festival, in the evening
Good to know: The lantern area spreads over Lương Nhữ Học, Hải Thượng Lãn Ông and Phú Định streets, where handmade lantern-making has been passed down through generations.

## Luc Ky Noodles (Lục Ký (hủ tiếu mì xá xíu)) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/luc-ky-noodles/
Type: Egg noodles & wontons · Area: Cholon (District 5)
Address: 103 Lê Hồng Phong, Phường Chợ Quán
About: Egg noodles with char siu pork, and noodles with chicken and dried fish, in District 5.
Hours: Open 24 hours

## No. 1 Tan Da Antique Café (Cà phê số 1 Tản Đà) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/no-1-tan-da-antique-cafe/
Type: Café · Area: Cholon (District 5)
Address: Số 1 Tản Đà, Quận 5 cũ
About: Café filled with antiques and gemstones, where collectors meet to trade.

## Phung Hung Market (Chợ Phùng Hưng) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/phung-hung-market/
Type: Local market · Area: Cholon (District 5)
Address: Góc Phùng Hưng – Nguyễn Trãi, Quận 5 cũ
About: Morning market in the heart of Cholon. Try sticky rice, steamed buns, Hong Kong-style rice rolls, chive cakes and old-school sock-filtered coffee. Busiest 6–9am.
Hours: Busiest 6am – 9am
What to order: Sticky rice from the Lan Anh stall (20,000–25,000 dong; the vendor has sold here for 49 years), Hong Kong-style rice rolls with pork, shrimp, scallop or crab (28,000–47,000 dong), Ba Lù coffee, Tăng bánh mì and the stuffed bitter melon and chilli stall
Good to know: Locals also call it chợ Thủ Đô or the "rich people's market".

## Phuong's Noodle Shop (Quán Phượng (bún riêu, hủ tiếu)) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/phuong-s-noodle-shop/
Type: Hu tieu noodle soup · Area: Cholon (District 5)
Address: Quận 5 cũ
About: District 5 shop serving both crab-and-tomato noodle soup (bun rieu) and hu tieu noodles.
What to order: Both bún riêu (crab and tomato noodles) and hủ tiếu

## Pork Rib Noodle Soup, Bui Huu Nghia (Bánh canh sườn cây Bùi Hữu Nghĩa) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/pork-rib-noodle-soup-bui-huu-nghia/
Type: Thick noodle soup · Area: Cholon (District 5)
Address: Bùi Hữu Nghĩa, Quận 5 cũ
About: Thick-noodle soup (banh canh) topped with giant pork ribs, made famous after a celebrity recommendation.
What to order: Bánh canh sườn cây: thick noodle soup with very large pork rib pieces and daikon
Good to know: Became popular after a review by the Vietnamese comedian Trấn Thành.

## Sam Ky Herbal Duck Noodles (Mì vịt tiềm Sâm Ký) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/sam-ky-herbal-duck-noodles/
Type: Herbal duck noodles · Area: Cholon (District 5)
Address: Quận 5 cũ
About: Herbal-braised duck with egg noodles in District 5.

## Thiem Huy Noodles (Thiêm Huy Mì Gia) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/thiem-huy-noodles/
Type: Egg noodles & wontons · Area: Cholon (District 5)
Address: 455 Nguyễn Trãi, Quận 5 cũ
About: Started as a street cart nearly 50 years ago. A favourite for herbal duck noodles, at 455 Nguyen Trai.

## Thuan Phat Chinese Stir-fry (Quán Thuận Phát (món Hoa chiên xào)) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/thuan-phat-chinese-stir-fry/
Type: Chinese-Vietnamese kitchen · Area: Cholon (District 5)
Address: Quận 5 cũ

## Vegetarian Noodles, 124B Ngo Nhan Tinh (Hủ tiếu chay 124B Ngô Nhân Tịnh) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/vegetarian-noodles-124b-ngo-nhan-tinh/
Type: Vegetarian · Area: Cholon (District 5)
Address: 124B Ngô Nhân Tịnh, Quận 5 cũ
About: Huge pot of vegetarian noodle soup with napa cabbage and lotus seeds, served on the 1st and 15th of the lunar month, 6–9am. Expect queues.
Hours: Only on the 1st and 15th days of the lunar month, from 6am until about 9am
Price: About 35,000 dong
What to order: Vegetarian hủ tiếu with napa cabbage and lotus seeds
Good to know: Very busy on those days; check a lunar calendar before you go.

## Vinh Phat Hong Kong Duck Noodles (Mì vịt tiềm Vĩnh Phát Hong Kong) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/vinh-phat-hong-kong-duck-noodles/
Type: Herbal duck noodles · Area: Cholon (District 5)
Address: 866 Nguyễn Chí Thanh, Quận 5 cũ
About: Hong Kong-style herbal duck noodles at 866 Nguyen Chi Thanh.
What to order: Hong Kong-style mì vịt tiềm (herbal duck noodles); a good evening stop

## Yukii Desserts (Yukii Desserts) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/yukii-desserts/
Type: Sweet soup desserts · Area: Cholon (District 5)
Address: Quận 5 cũ
About: Chinese sweet-soup shop with pretty, photogenic desserts, including lotus-shaped sweets and a strawberry snow ice.
What to order: Chinese-style chè, the lotus-flower dessert and the strawberry snow ice

## Binh Tay Market (Chợ Bình Tây) — https://hcmcinsider.com/places/binh-tay-market/
Type: Local market · Area: Cholon (District 6)
Address: Quận 6 cũ
About: Cholon's century-old wholesale market. A busy, colourful place to see Chinatown trading life.
What to order: Bún thịt nướng (grilled pork noodles) and chè nhãn nhục (longan sweet soup) from the market stalls

# SIGHTS
## Cu Chi Tunnels (Địa đạo Củ Chi) — https://hcmcinsider.com/see-and-do/cu-chi-tunnels/
Area: Cu Chi (outer Ho Chi Minh City)
Addr: Bến Đình (xã Nhuận Đức) hoặc Bến Dược (xã An Nhơn Tây), Củ Chi cũ, TP.HCM
Short: Yes, if you want to understand the war from the Vietnamese side. The tunnels are about 70 km from the city centre, so the real question is how you get there: a half-day tour is easiest, the public bus is cheap but slow. There are two sites, Ben Dinh (closer, busier) and Ben Duoc (further, quieter).
Hours: 7:00 am – 5:00 pm daily
Entry: About 125,000 dong for foreign adults; check the board at the gate
Time needed: Half a day including travel; 1.5–2 hours on site
Which site: Ben Dinh: closer and set up for tours. Ben Duoc: further, quieter, with a memorial temple
Why go: A network of about 250 km of tunnels dug from 1948 and joined into one system in the 1960s, with kitchens, meeting rooms and field hospitals underground. You can crawl through a short, widened section, see hidden trapdoors and booby traps, and taste steamed cassava, the wartime staple. It is one of Vietnam's most visited sites and ranks among Tripadvisor's top attractions in Asia (CafeF, June 2026).
Tips: Start early: mornings are cooler and the busiest tour groups arrive late morning. Wear clothes you don't mind getting dusty, closed shoes and insect repellent. The tunnels are tight and dark: skip the crawl if you are claustrophobic; there is plenty to see above ground. A shooting range on site sells bullets for real wartime rifles; it is loud and optional.
Getting there: Half-day tour from District 1 (by bus, or by speedboat on the Saigon River): the easiest option, ticket and guide usually included. Public bus to Ben Duoc: bus 13 from Saigon bus station to Cu Chi bus station, then bus 79. Allow 2+ hours each way; city buses are free until 31 Dec 2026. From Cholon: bus 94 from Cholon bus station to Cu Chi, then bus 79. Ride-hailing car: about 1.5–2 hours each way depending on traffic; agree on a wait-and-return if you book by the hour.
Facts last checked: 2026-10-30

## War Remnants Museum (Bảo tàng Chứng tích Chiến tranh) — https://hcmcinsider.com/see-and-do/war-remnants-museum/
Area: District 3 (city centre)
Addr: 28 Võ Văn Tần, phường Xuân Hòa (Quận 3 cũ), TP.HCM
Short: Yes, it is the city's most visited museum and the clearest introduction to the war's human cost. Some galleries, especially on Agent Orange, are very graphic: plan two hours and some quiet time afterwards. Tickets are cheap and can now be bought online to skip the queue.
Hours: 7:30 am – 5:30 pm daily; ticket counter closes 5:00 pm
Entry: 40,000 dong; students half price; under-6s free
Time needed: 1.5–2 hours
Tickets online: ticket.baotangchungtichchientranh.vn
Why go: Photo galleries by war photographers from many countries, including those who died covering the conflict. Tanks, aircraft and artillery in the courtyard, and a reconstruction of the 'tiger cage' prison cells. A 10-minute walk from the Independence Palace, so the two fit into one morning.
Tips: Go at opening time: tour groups fill the galleries from mid-morning. Start on the top floor and work down; the hardest galleries are on the upper floors and you can skip them. It may not suit young children; parents often see the courtyard and ground floor only.
Getting there: Walk: about 15 minutes from Ben Thanh Market, 10 minutes from the Independence Palace. Metro Line 1: Ben Thanh station, then walk about 15 minutes. Ride-hailing: ask for “Bảo tàng Chứng tích Chiến tranh”.
Facts last checked: 2026-10-30

## Independence Palace (Dinh Độc Lập) — https://hcmcinsider.com/see-and-do/independence-palace/
Area: District 1 (city centre)
Addr: 135 Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa, phường Bến Thành (Quận 1 cũ), TP.HCM
Short: Yes: it is where the war ended on 30 April 1975, when a tank broke through the gate, and the 1960s building is almost untouched inside. Allow 1–1.5 hours, go down to the basement command bunker, and pair it with the War Remnants Museum nearby.
Hours: Main building 8:00 am – 4:30 pm; exhibition 8:30 am – 4:30 pm; tickets until 3:30 pm
Entry: 40,000 dong (palace); 65,000 dong with the exhibition. Students 20,000 / 45,000
Time needed: 1–1.5 hours
Why go: A rare, well-kept piece of 1960s modernist architecture, with the original meeting rooms, banquet hall and furniture. The basement still holds the war-room maps, radio equipment and tunnels of the presidential bunker. Replicas of the tanks that entered on 30 April 1975 stand in the grounds.
Tips: Arrive before 3:00 pm; the last ticket is sold at 3:30 pm. Don't skip the basement: the bunker is the most atmospheric part. Signs inside are short; a guided city tour or reading up beforehand adds a lot of context.
Getting there: Walk: about 10 minutes from Ben Thanh Market or Notre-Dame Cathedral. Metro Line 1: Ben Thanh station, then about 10 minutes on foot. Ride-hailing: ask for “Dinh Độc Lập”; the visitor entrance is on Nam Ky Khoi Nghia street.
Facts last checked: 2026-10-30

## Mekong Delta day trip (Du lịch miền Tây: Mỹ Tho – Bến Tre) — https://hcmcinsider.com/see-and-do/mekong-delta-day-trip/
Area: My Tho and Ben Tre (Mekong Delta)
Addr: Bến tàu Mỹ Tho và các cồn Thới Sơn, Cồn Phụng trên sông Tiền
Short: Yes, if you want a taste of river life without staying overnight. A day trip to My Tho and Ben Tre means about two hours on the road each way, then boats between coconut-palm islands, fruit, honey tea and folk music. It is touristy but pleasant; for real floating markets you need to stay a night near Can Tho.
Time needed: A full day, roughly 7:00 am – 5:00 pm
Travel: About 2 hours each way by road
Best for: A first look at the delta without staying overnight
Floating markets: Not on most day trips; Cai Rang (Can Tho) needs an overnight stay
Why go: A boat ride on the wide Tien River past the 'four sacred animal' islands and the Rach Mieu bridge. Paddling a small sampan through narrow coconut-palm canals, the photo everyone comes for. Coconut candy workshops, honey tea, tropical fruit and đờn ca tài tử, the traditional music of the south.
Tips: Bring sunscreen, a hat and insect repellent; boats have little shade. Carry small notes for tips to the sampan rowers and musicians. Small-group tours visit the same islands but feel much less crowded.
Getting there: Day tour with hotel or District 1 pickup: by far the easiest, with boats, lunch and guide included. Combined Cu Chi Tunnels + Mekong day tours exist but are rushed; pick one if you can. Going alone: intercity buses leave from the Mien Tay bus station; you then arrange boats at My Tho pier yourself.
Facts last checked: 2026-10-30

## Landmark 81 SkyView (Đài quan sát Landmark 81 SkyView) — https://hcmcinsider.com/see-and-do/landmark-81-skyview/
Area: Binh Thanh (east of the centre)
Addr: Landmark 81, Vinhomes Central Park, Nguyễn Hữu Cảnh, phường Thạnh Mỹ Tây (Bình Thạnh cũ)
Short: Yes, for the highest view in the city: the observation deck is on floors 79–81 of Vietnam's tallest building. Go late afternoon to see sunset and the lights come on, and come by metro to Tan Cang station. Tickets are pricier at weekends, so a weekday visit saves money.
Hours: 9:00 am – 10:00 pm
Entry: About 420,000 dong weekdays, 500,000 dong weekends (adult combo)
Time needed: 1–1.5 hours
Best time: 4:00 pm onwards for sunset and night views
Why go: 360° views over the Saigon River, District 1's skyline and the new Thu Thiem area. A glass floor, telescopes and the 'Skytouch' open-air challenge on the top floor, with safety gear. Bars and restaurants on floor 79 if you want to stay for a drink after dark.
Tips: Check the weather: on hazy or rainy days the view drops a lot. Drinking water and dangerous items are not allowed in; finish your drink before security. Weekday tickets are cheaper and the deck is quieter.
Getting there: Metro Line 1: Tan Cang station, then a short walk to Vinhomes Central Park. Ride-hailing: ask for “Landmark 81”, about 20–25 minutes from Ben Thanh depending on traffic. Ticket counter: basement B1 of Vincom Landmark 81.
Facts last checked: 2026-10-30

## Saigon River dinner cruise (Du thuyền ăn tối trên sông Sài Gòn) — https://hcmcinsider.com/see-and-do/saigon-river-dinner-cruise/
Area: District 1 and District 4 riverfront
Addr: Các bến du thuyền dọc sông Sài Gòn (Quận 1, Quận 4 cũ)
Short: Worth it if you want an easy, relaxed evening: two hours on the river with dinner and the lit-up skyline. The food is buffet or set menus rather than the city's best, so treat it as a view with dinner. Book ahead for weekends and holidays.
Times: Board around 6:30–7:00 pm, back around 9:00–9:30 pm
Price: From about 500,000 dong per person (buffet); more for upper decks and fine dining
Time needed: About 2.5 hours
Often extra: Drinks, VAT, service charge
Why go: The best way to see the skyline at night, including Landmark 81 and the Thu Thiem bridges. Buffet or set-menu dinner on board, often with live music. A calm break from motorbike traffic, good for families and couples.
Tips: Check exactly what is included: drinks, VAT and transfers vary a lot between boats. Ask for an upper or outdoor deck for the best views. Bring a light layer: it can be windy on deck.
Getting there: Piers are in District 1 (around Bach Dang) and District 4 (near Nha Rong wharf); your ticket names the exact pier. Ride-hailing is easiest; arrive 30 minutes before departure. On a budget, the river bus from Bach Dang pier gives similar views for a fraction of the price (no dinner).
Facts last checked: 2026-10-30

## Saigon Notre-Dame Cathedral (Nhà thờ Chính tòa Đức Bà Sài Gòn) — https://hcmcinsider.com/see-and-do/notre-dame-cathedral-saigon/
Area: District 1 (city centre)
Addr: 01 Công xã Paris, phường Sài Gòn (Quận 1 cũ)
Short: Yes, go, but mostly for the outside for now. The red-brick cathedral has been under a major restoration since 2017 and is wrapped in scaffolding; inside access has been limited to Mass and registered groups. It sits right next to the Central Post Office, so see both in one stop.
Inside: Mass (5:30 am and 5:30 pm daily, as of Dec 2025) and registered groups; general visits not yet reopened
Outside: Free, any time
Time needed: 20–30 minutes, more with the Post Office
Why go: Built from 1877 to 1880 with materials shipped from Europe, it is Saigon's best-known colonial landmark and still a working cathedral. In March 2026 two gilded crosses, each about 3.7 m tall and 400 kg, were lifted to the top of the bell tower, one of the restoration's big milestones. The square in front, with the statue of the Virgin Mary, is a classic photo spot and a short walk from Nguyen Hue and Ben Thanh Market.
Tips: Come early morning or late afternoon for softer light and fewer tour groups. If you go in for Mass, cover shoulders and knees and stay quiet; photos during services are not appropriate. The square is ringed by busy traffic: cross with the steady, slow walk locals use.
Getting there: Metro Line 1: Opera House station, about a 10-minute walk. City buses are free until 31 Dec 2026; many routes stop around Ben Thanh, about 15 minutes on foot. Ride-hailing: ask for “Nhà thờ Đức Bà”.
Facts last checked: 2026-10-24

## Saigon Central Post Office (Bưu điện Trung tâm Sài Gòn) — https://hcmcinsider.com/see-and-do/saigon-central-post-office/
Area: District 1 (city centre)
Addr: 2 Công xã Paris, phường Sài Gòn (Quận 1 cũ)
Short: Yes. It is free, open every day from about 7 am to 7 pm, and right next to the Notre-Dame Cathedral. Step inside for the vaulted hall, old maps and wooden phone booths, and send a postcard from a post office that still works.
Hours: About 7:00 am – 7:00 pm daily, including most holidays (checked January 2026)
Entry: Free
Time needed: 20–30 minutes
Why go: Built between 1886 and 1891, it is usually credited to the architect Alfred Foulhoux. The popular story that Gustave Eiffel designed it has no documentary evidence. The main hall has a steel-ribbed glass vault, a clock over the entrance and two hand-drawn 19th-century maps on the walls. Rows of wooden public telephone booths still line the hall, and you can buy stamps and post cards home.
Tips: Mornings are calmer before tour buses arrive. Souvenir stalls inside are convenient but not the cheapest; compare before buying. Hours can shift slightly around Tết and national holidays.
Getting there: Next door to the Notre-Dame Cathedral. Metro Line 1: Opera House station, about a 10-minute walk. Ride-hailing: ask for “Bưu điện Thành phố”.
Facts last checked: 2026-10-24

## Nguyen Hue Walking Street and the Opera House (Phố đi bộ Nguyễn Huệ · Nhà hát Thành phố) — https://hcmcinsider.com/see-and-do/nguyen-hue-walking-street/
Area: District 1 (city centre)
Addr: Đường Nguyễn Huệ, phường Sài Gòn (Quận 1 cũ)
Short: Yes, go in the evening. The pedestrian boulevard runs about 670 m from the City Hall area down towards the Saigon River, is free and open around the clock, and is at its liveliest after dark, especially at weekends. The Opera House is a few minutes' walk away on Le Loi.
Hours: Open 24 hours
Entry: Free
Opera House: Outside free; shows are ticketed
Time needed: 45 minutes to an evening
Why go: The central section became a pedestrian square around 2015 and is now Saigon's main open-air living room: families, skaters, buskers and dancers by the fountain in the evening. A large bronze statue of Ho Chi Minh stands at the top end in front of the colonial City Hall; the other end opens towards the river. Early mornings are for locals: tai chi, badminton and runners from about 6:30 to 8:00 am. Around Lunar New Year the street turns into the Tết flower street, one of the city's biggest seasonal displays.
Tips: Come after sunset when it is cooler and the buildings are lit. Keep your phone away from the kerb side: snatching from passing motorbikes happens in busy areas. Many cafés sit in the old apartment blocks along the street; look for the stairwells with café signs.
Getting there: Metro Line 1: Opera House station, a few minutes' walk. From Ben Thanh Market, walk east along Le Loi for about 10 minutes. Walk to the river end for Bach Dang pier, where the river bus leaves.
Facts last checked: 2026-10-24

## Ben Thanh Market (Chợ Bến Thành) — https://hcmcinsider.com/see-and-do/ben-thanh-market/
Area: District 1 (city centre)
Addr: Chợ Bến Thành, phường Bến Thành (Quận 1 cũ)
Short: Worth a look for the building and the food stalls, but it is the city's most touristy market: prices for souvenirs start high. The market runs from about 6 am to 6 pm, then a night market sets up on the side streets until about 10 pm. Metro Line 1 starts right next to it.
Hours: About 6:00 am – 6:00 pm; night market on the side streets until about 10:00 pm
Entry: Free
Time needed: 45–90 minutes
Why go: The current building with its famous clock tower was finished in 1914 and is one of Saigon's symbols. Inside you will find clothes, coffee, dried fruit and a food section where you can try many Vietnamese dishes under one roof. After 6 pm, stalls on Phan Bội Châu and Phan Chu Trinh streets add an evening market with more food.
Tips: Ask the price before you order or buy, and bargain politely for souvenirs. Crowds attract pickpockets: carry your bag in front. For more local markets, head to Cholon: Binh Tay, Phung Hung and Hoa Binh.
Getting there: Metro Line 1: Ben Thanh station is right next to the market. Airport bus 152 runs via Ben Thanh Market; city buses are free until 31 Dec 2026. Ride-hailing: ask for “Chợ Bến Thành”.
Facts last checked: 2026-10-24

## Thien Hau Temple (Tue Thanh Assembly Hall) (Chùa Bà Thiên Hậu · Hội quán Tuệ Thành) — https://hcmcinsider.com/see-and-do/thien-hau-temple-cholon/
Area: Cholon (District 5)
Addr: 710 Nguyễn Trãi, phường Chợ Lớn (Quận 5 cũ)
Short: Yes, it is one of the most atmospheric temples in Cholon. The Cantonese community's assembly hall honours Thiên Hậu, goddess of the sea, and is known for its ceramic roof figures and giant hanging incense coils. Open daily about 6:30 am to 4:30 pm.
Hours: About 6:30 am – 4:30 pm
Festival: Vía Bà, 22nd–24th day of the 3rd lunar month (very crowded)
Time needed: 30 minutes
Why go: Founded by Chinese families from Guangzhou (Tuệ Thành), it was already recorded around 1820; inscriptions on its bell and incense burner date to 1830. The roof, walls and eaves are lined with ceramic figures telling Chinese stories, and the central courtyard light well lets sun fall through the incense smoke. People hang spiral incense coils that burn for days as prayers; the temple keeps hundreds of antique pieces.
Tips: Dress modestly, speak softly and ask before photographing people praying. Do not touch altars or offerings; donations are welcome. Mornings are quieter and the light through the courtyard is best.
Getting there: Ride-hailing from District 1 takes about 20–30 minutes depending on traffic. City bus 1 runs from the centre to Cholon (free until 31 Dec 2026). Combine with Lantern Street, the herbal medicine street and Phung Hung Market nearby.
Facts last checked: 2026-10-24

## Binh Tay Market (Chợ Bình Tây) — https://hcmcinsider.com/see-and-do/binh-tay-market/
Area: Cholon (District 6)
Addr: 57A Tháp Mười, phường Bình Tây (Quận 6 cũ)
Short: Yes, it is Cholon's grand old market and far more local than Ben Thanh. Come in the morning for the wholesale bustle and breakfast stalls, or in the evening for the Cholon night street of food stalls around the market (daily 6 pm to midnight).
Day market: Busiest in the early morning
Night street: Daily 6:00 pm – midnight around the market
Time needed: 1 hour, more if you eat
Why go: Built in 1928 and opened in 1930, it was funded by the merchant Quách Đàm, whose statue stands in the courtyard. Its Chinese-style roofs make it one of Saigon's most photogenic buildings. It is a working wholesale market: dried goods, spices, kitchenware and snacks sold by the sack. Since December 2025 the Phố đêm Chợ Lớn night street fills the four streets around the market with food stalls and food trucks every evening.
Tips: Inside the market, try bún thịt nướng and chè nhãn nhục (longan sweet soup), as recommended in creators' videos. Wholesale stalls may not sell single items; snack and souvenir stalls do. Keep bags zipped in the crowded aisles.
Getting there: City bus 1 ends at Cholon bus station near the market (free until 31 Dec 2026). Ride-hailing from District 1 takes about 25–35 minutes depending on traffic. Ask for “Chợ Bình Tây”.
Facts last checked: 2026-10-24

# EVENTS AND FESTIVALS
## Chợ Lớn Food Story 2026 (Lễ hội Ẩm thực Chợ Lớn Food Story 2026) — https://hcmcinsider.com/events/cho-lon-food-story/
Area: Cholon (old District 5)
Addr: 105 Trần Hưng Đạo, phường An Đông, TP.HCM
Short: Yes, if you are in Saigon from 4 to 6 December 2026. Cholon's yearly food festival brings about 60 stalls of Vietnamese and Chinese-Vietnamese (Hoa) dishes under one roof, with cooking demos, lion and dragon dancing at the opening and music in the evenings. It is the easiest way to taste Chinatown in one evening.
Dates: 2026-12-04 to 2026-12-06
Dates: Fri 4 – Sun 6 December 2026
Hours: From 9:00 am on 4 Dec (opening 6:00 pm); 7:00 am – 9:30 pm on 5–6 Dec
Where: 105 Tran Hung Dao, An Dong Ward (Cholon)
Stalls: About 60, Vietnamese and Hoa food
Why go: About 60 stalls of Vietnamese and Hoa (Chinese-Vietnamese) dishes from Cholon's kitchens. Opening night on Friday 4 December at 6:00 pm, with festival drums, lion dance and dragon dance. Saturday 5 December: a hands-on session cooking signature Hoa dishes (2:00–4:00 pm) and a bicycle parade in the morning (8:00–9:00 am, planned). Taste-and-guess games, and Vietnamese and Chinese music with acoustic sets in the evenings. This year's theme is 'Bát Bửu – Sắc vị tinh hoa', the Eight Treasures, a nod to the lucky number 8.
Tips: Weekend evenings are the busiest; go on Friday daytime or in the mornings for shorter queues. Bring small cash notes; not every stall takes cards. Share dishes so you can try more stalls. The festival is one weekend only; the rest of the year, Cholon's family shops are open daily.
Getting there: Ride-hailing: ask for “105 Trần Hưng Đạo, phường An Đông”. Bus 1 runs from the city centre towards Cholon; city buses are free until 31 Dec 2026. Combine it with Cholon's old shops: see the Cholon food guide for places nearby.
Facts last checked: 2026-10-30

## Lantern Festival in Cholon (Tết Nguyên Tiêu) (Tết Nguyên Tiêu của người Hoa Chợ Lớn) — https://hcmcinsider.com/events/tet-nguyen-tieu-cholon/
Area: Cholon (old District 5)
Addr: Các hội quán và đường phố khu Chợ Lớn (phường An Đông, Chợ Lớn)
Short: Yes: it is Cholon's biggest night of the year and a national intangible heritage. On the 15th day of the first lunar month (Saturday 20 February 2027) the Chinese community's assembly halls light up, lion and dragon troupes fill the streets and a huge parade winds through Chinatown. Expect big crowds and go early.
Dates: 2027-02-20 to 2027-02-20
Next date: Saturday 20 February 2027 (15th day, 1st lunar month)
Where: Cholon: assembly halls on Nguyen Trai and Tran Hung Dao, parade streets around Hai Thuong Lan Ong and Luong Nhu Hoc
Cost: Free to watch
Heritage: National intangible cultural heritage (2020)
Why go: A street parade with lion, dragon and unicorn troupes, giant drums, the Eight Immortals and stilt walkers; in 2026 about 1,200 performers took part. Cholon's old assembly halls (hội quán), such as Nghia An on Nguyen Trai street, hold rituals and lantern offerings, and some carry their deity through the neighbourhood. An evening show at the An Dong Ward Public Service Centre, 105 Tran Hung Dao, broadcast on HTV. The customs of the Lantern Festival of Cholon's Chinese community have been on Vietnam's national intangible heritage list since 2020.
Tips: Pick a spot along the route 30–45 minutes before the parade starts. Keep your phone and bag close; crowds are dense. Lion troupes 'pick' red envelopes and greens hung outside shops for luck: watch, but leave space for them. Assembly halls are working places of worship: dress modestly and ask before photographing rituals.
Getting there: Ride-hailing to Nguyen Trai or Tran Hung Dao in Cholon; expect road closures along the parade route. Walk the last stretch: streets near the parade are packed. Bus 1 from the city centre stops in Cholon.
Facts last checked: 2026-10-30

## Lion and dragon dance in Saigon (Múa lân – sư – rồng) — https://hcmcinsider.com/events/lion-dragon-dance-saigon/
Area: Cholon and across the city
Addr: Khu Chợ Lớn và các tuyến phố khắp TP.HCM
Short: Yes, if your trip falls on the right dates. Lion (lân), lion (sư, the northern Chinese style) and dragon (rồng) troupes perform for luck at the Lunar New Year, the Lantern Festival and the Mid-Autumn Festival, and at shop openings all year. Cholon, Saigon's Chinatown, has the most troupes and the best chance of seeing one.
When: Lunar New Year, Lantern Festival (20 Feb 2027), Mid-Autumn Festival, shop openings
Where: Cholon streets and assembly halls; malls and hotels at Tet
Cost: Free to watch
Sound: Loud drums: bring ear plugs for small children
Why go: Drums, cymbals and gongs set the rhythm while two dancers inside each lion leap, bow and 'sleep'; acrobatic troupes balance on tall poles. The lion 'plucks the greens' (lettuce and a red envelope hung over a door) to bring luck to the shop or home. Dragons are carried on poles by a team of dancers, chasing a pearl through the street. Some Cholon troupes also bring out the Ông Địa (Earth God) character, who fans and teases the lion.
Tips: Follow the drums: you will usually hear a troupe before you see it. Don't step between the lion and the greens it is trying to reach. Small red envelopes (lì xì) for the troupe are welcome but not expected from visitors.
Getting there: Cholon is 20–30 minutes from District 1 by car; bus 1 also goes there. At Tet, malls and big hotels in District 1 often book troupes in the first days of the year. For the biggest show, follow the Lantern Festival parade in Cholon.
Facts last checked: 2026-10-30

## Tết (Lunar New Year) in Saigon 2027 (Tết Nguyên Đán Đinh Mùi 2027) — https://hcmcinsider.com/events/tet-vietnamese-new-year/
Area: Citywide
Addr: TP. Hồ Chí Minh
Short: Yes, with planning. The first day of the Year of the Goat (Đinh Mùi) is Saturday 6 February 2027. The week before is festive and busy; then for the first days of the new year the city empties out, many family shops close and the streets are calm and decorated. Book transport and rooms early, and expect some places on this site to be closed.
Dates: 2027-02-06 to 2027-02-08
New Year's Day: Saturday 6 February 2027
New Year's Eve: Friday 5 February 2027
Busiest travel: The week before Tet
Quietest days: The first 3 days of the new year
Why go: The days before Tet: flower markets, kumquat and apricot-blossom trees on every motorbike, and streets hung with red lanterns. New Year's Eve (the night of 5 February 2027): the city usually holds fireworks at several sites at midnight. The first days of the year: quiet streets, people in new clothes visiting pagodas and family, and lion dances for luck. Two weeks later, the Lantern Festival (20 February 2027) brings Cholon's biggest parade.
Tips: Check opening days before crossing town to a restaurant; many family shops close over the first days. Say “Chúc mừng năm mới” (Happy New Year) to the people you meet. Give and receive red envelopes (lì xì) with both hands; new, crisp notes are the custom. Avoid sweeping, arguing or lending money on the first day; locals take first-day luck seriously.
Getting there: Book flights, trains and buses out of the city weeks ahead; they sell out before Tet. Ride-hailing still works over Tet, but expect higher prices and longer waits. Arriving around Tet? Pre-book your airport transfer; see the airport to city guide.
Facts last checked: 2026-10-30

# PRACTICAL GUIDES
## https://hcmcinsider.com/guides/where-to-stay-ho-chi-minh-city/
Planning · Where to stay
 Where to stay in Ho Chi Minh City: the best areas for visitors
 Saigon is big and traffic is slow, so where you sleep decides how much of your trip is spent in a car. Here are the four areas we would pick, who each one suits, and the catch with each.
 Short answer: first visit of 2–4 days, stay in District 1 near Ben Thanh or the Opera House, but a few blocks away from Bui Vien. Want a quieter base that is still central, pick District 3 . Here mainly to eat, stay in Cholon . Staying a week or more, or with kids, look at Thao Dien . Not sure? Take the 30-second quiz .
 The four areas compared
 District 1 (Ben Thanh, Nguyen Hue)
 Best for: First visit, short stays, walking to the sights
 Walk to Ben Thanh Market, Nguyen Hue, the Opera House, Notre-Dame and the Post Office.
 Metro Line 1 starts here (Ben Thanh and Opera House stations), and airport bus 152 stops at Ben Thanh.
 Widest choice of hotels, from hostels to five-star riverside towers.
 Keep in mind: Busiest and priciest area. Streets around Bui Vien (the backpacker quarter) are loud until late: pick a hotel a few blocks away if you want to sleep.
 District 3
 Best for: A quieter base next to the centre
 Leafy streets, old villas and local cafés, 10–20 minutes on foot from District 1.
 Close to the War Remnants Museum and the Independence Palace.
 Often better value than District 1 for similar hotels.
 Keep in mind: Fewer big hotels; more boutique and serviced-apartment style. Nightlife is limited compared with District 1.
 Cholon (Districts 5, 6 and 11)
 Best for: Food lovers and repeat visitors
 Saigon's Chinatown, where most of the food spots on this site are.
 Temples, Binh Tay Market and old trade streets on your doorstep.
 Hotels are noticeably cheaper than in District 1.
 Keep in mind: About 20–30 minutes by car from District 1; the metro does not reach Cholon yet (bus 1 does). Little English and few international-style hotels.
 Thao Dien (Thu Duc)
 Best for: Longer stays, families, a calmer pace
 The expat quarter: cafés, brunch spots, boutiques and riverside restaurants.
 Metro Line 1 (Thao Dien station) reaches Ben Thanh in about 15 minutes.
 More space, green streets and serviced apartments for longer stays.
 Keep in mind: Far from Cholon and the old-town sights. Fewer budget options.
 Tips for booking
 Check the map, not the name: many hotels call themselves "District 1" while being a long walk from the sights.
 Ask for a room away from the street side if you are a light sleeper; motorbike traffic starts early.
 Near a metro station is a real plus for getting east to Thao Dien and Landmark 81.
 Arriving late? Book an airport transfer to the hotel door.
 Plan the rest
 Airport to city Metro guide See & Do Cholon food guide

## https://hcmcinsider.com/guides/arriving-in-saigon/
Arriving · Tan Son Nhat (SGN)
 Tan Son Nhat airport to District 1: transfers, Grab, taxi and bus
 The airport is only about 7 km from the city centre, but traffic can make it 20 minutes or an hour. Here is how to get into town, get online and get cash, sorted from easiest to cheapest.
 Short answer: late at night, with luggage or kids, book a fixed-price transfer . Otherwise install an eSIM before you fly and order a ride-hailing car when you land. On a budget in daytime, bus 152 to Ben Thanh is free until the end of 2026.
 Which terminal?
 Terminal 2 · international
 Most visitors arrive here
 Bus 152 stops at T1/T2 (daytime)
 Terminal 3 · domestic
 Flights within Vietnam
 Bus 109 runs from T3 to Saigon bus station, 5:30 am – 10:40 pm
 Your options into the city
 1 · Pre-booked transfer
 Fixed price agreed in advance; the driver waits in arrivals with your name
 Best for late flights, families and big luggage
 Book an airport transfer ↗ 
 2 · Ride-hailing app
 Grab, Xanh SM and Be work like Uber; you see the price before you book
 Follow the signs to the app pickup area outside arrivals
 You need mobile data on landing: an eSIM solves this
 3 · Metered taxi
 Use the official taxi rank outside arrivals
 Check the meter is on; ignore touts inside the hall
 4 · Bus (cheapest)
 Bus 152: T1/T2 → Ben Thanh Market, daytime only
 Bus 109: T3 → Saigon bus station, until about 10:40 pm
 Free until 31 Dec 2026: tap a contactless card or phone when boarding. Bus guide 
 Get online the moment you land
 eSIM (easiest)
 Buy and install before your flight; switch it on after landing
 No queue, no passport registration at a kiosk, keep your home SIM for calls
 Vietnam eSIMs on Airalo ↗ · Saily ↗ 
 Local SIM card
 Kiosks of the big networks in the arrivals hall
 Bring your passport: SIM cards must be registered to an ID
 Works on any unlocked phone
 Cash and cards
 ATMs are in the arrivals hall; take out enough dong for street food and small shops, which are often cash-only.
 Cards and phone payments work in malls, hotels, the metro and on buses.
 Keep small notes (10,000–100,000 dong) for taxis and stalls.
 What visitors filmed here
 Chaotic Arrival In Saigon, Vietnam 🇻🇳 YouTube · Ken Abroad · 290.6K views 
 Videos by travellers, linked to their original YouTube channels. View counts as of October 2026.
 Questions visitors ask
 How do I get from Tan Son Nhat airport to District 1?
 The easiest options are a pre-booked transfer (fixed price, driver waiting with your name) or a ride-hailing car from the app pickup area. On a budget, take bus 152 from the international terminal (daytime) to Ben Thanh Market; city buses are free until 31 December 2026.
 Which terminal will I arrive at?
 International flights use Terminal 2 (T2). Most domestic flights use the newer Terminal 3 (T3). Bus 152 serves T1/T2; bus 109 serves T3.
 Does the metro go to the airport?
 No. Metro Line 1 runs from Ben Thanh to Suoi Tien, in the opposite direction. Take a bus, taxi or ride-hailing car to the city first.
 Should I get an eSIM or a local SIM card?
 If your phone supports eSIM, install one before you fly and turn it on when you land: you have data for the ride-hailing app straight away. Local SIM cards are sold in the arrivals hall but need your passport for registration and there can be a queue.
 Are airport taxis safe?
 Use the official taxi rank outside arrivals or a ride-hailing app, and ignore people offering rides inside the hall. Make sure the meter is on before you set off.

## https://hcmcinsider.com/guides/hcmc-metro/
Getting around
 Ho Chi Minh City metro guide for visitors
 Metro Line 1 is the fastest way to cross the eastern half of the city: air-conditioned, cheap and easy to use with a contactless bank card. Here is everything a visitor needs, checked against official sources.
 Line 1 · Ben Thanh – Suoi Tien
 14 stations, about 20 km, roughly 30 minutes end to end. Orange dots are the stops most visitors use.
 Ben Thanh underground Ben Thanh Market, Bui Vien Street, Tao Dan Park 
 Opera House underground Opera House, Nguyen Hue walking street; Notre Dame and the Post Office a short walk away 
 Ba Son underground Bach Dang Wharf and the riverside park 
 Van Thanh Park 
 Tan Cang Landmark 81 and Vinhomes Central Park 
 Thao Dien Cafes, restaurants and boutiques of the expat quarter 
 An Phu Vincom Mega Mall 
 Rach Chiec 
 Phuoc Long 
 Binh Thai 
 Thu Duc Thu Duc Market 
 High-Tech Park 
 National University 
 Suoi Tien Bus Station End of the line; Suoi Tien Theme Park is nearby 
 Hours
 Mon–Fri: 5:00 am – 10:00 pm
 Weekends and holidays: until 11:00 pm
 Every 6–8 min at rush hour, 10–12 min otherwise
 Fares
 Single trip: 7,000–20,000 dong cash, 1,000 less by card or app
 1-day pass: 40,000 dong
 3-day pass: 90,000 dong
 How to pay
 Tap your bank card or phone at the gate (Visa, Mastercard, JCB, Amex, UnionPay, Apple Pay, Samsung Pay). Use the same card to tap out.
 Ticket machines take cash (1,000–200,000 dong notes) and issue a card with a refundable deposit.
 HCMC Metro app: buy a ticket and scan the QR code.
 Good to know
 No eating, drinking or smoking in stations or on trains; no pets.
 Large or bulky luggage may be refused. A carry-on is fine.
 Line 1 does not go to the airport or Cholon yet. Line 2 (Ben Thanh – Tham Luong) started construction in January 2026.
 Questions visitors ask
 How much does the Ho Chi Minh City metro cost?
 A single trip costs 7,000–20,000 dong depending on distance, or 1,000 dong less when you pay by card or app. A 1-day pass is 40,000 dong and a 3-day pass is 90,000 dong.
 Can I pay with my foreign Visa or Mastercard?
 Yes. Contactless Visa, Mastercard, JCB, Amex and UnionPay cards, plus Apple Pay and Samsung Pay, work directly at the gates. Tap in and out with the same card or phone.
 What are the metro opening hours?
 Monday to Friday from 5:00 am to 10:00 pm; on weekends and public holidays until 11:00 pm. Trains run every 6–8 minutes at rush hour and every 10–12 minutes at other times.
 Does the metro go to the airport or Cholon?
 Not yet. Line 1 runs east from Ben Thanh to Suoi Tien. Line 2 (Ben Thanh – Tham Luong) started construction in January 2026. For the airport and Cholon, use a ride-hailing app, taxi or bus.

## https://hcmcinsider.com/guides/getting-around-hcmc/
Getting around
 Getting around Ho Chi Minh City: buses, airport and river bus
 City buses are free until the end of 2026, the airport has its own cheap bus lines, and the river bus is one of the nicest rides in Saigon. Here is what visitors need to know, checked against official announcements and Vietnamese news sources.
 Buses are free until 31 December 2026
 The city has waived fares on 134 bus routes. Since 1 October 2026, tap a contactless bank card or phone (Visa, Mastercard, Apple Pay, Google Pay, Samsung Pay) on the reader when you board. It only records the trip; nothing is charged.
 From the airport (Tan Son Nhat, SGN)
 Bus 152
 Airport → Ben Thanh Market → Trung Son
 The easiest bus to the city centre
 On the city's free-fare list until 31 Dec 2026
 Bus 109
 Airport → Saigon bus station (near Ben Thanh and 23/9 Park)
 On the city's free-fare list until 31 Dec 2026
 Bus stops are outside the arrivals halls; ask airport staff which terminal your bus serves. Late at night, use a ride-hailing app or a pre-booked transfer ↗ . All options compared: airport to city guide .
 City buses visitors use
 Bus 1 · to Cholon
 Ba Son metro station → city centre → Cholon bus station (Chinatown)
 Handy for the food spots on this site
 Bus 150 · Cholon to the east
 Cholon bus station → New Mien Dong bus station
 Crosses the city from Chinatown to the big new eastern bus station
 Bus 13 + 79 · Cu Chi Tunnels
 Bus 13: Saigon bus station → Cu Chi bus station
 Bus 79: Cu Chi bus station → Ben Duoc
 Slow: allow 2+ hours each way. Tours ↗ are easier. Cu Chi visitor guide 
 Bus 94 · Cholon to Cu Chi
 Cholon bus station → Cu Chi bus station
 An alternative start if you stay in Chinatown
 For routes and live arrival times, use the BusMap app or Google Maps. Wave clearly at the bus as it approaches; buses may not stop if nobody signals.
 Saigon river bus
 Route
 Bach Dang pier (District 1) → Binh An → Thanh Da → Hiep Binh Chanh → Linh Dong
 Great views of the skyline and the Saigon River
 Times and fares
 From 8:30 am daily, last departures in the evening
 About 15,000 dong per trip
 Tickets at the pier or online
 Sightseeing bus
 Open-top double-decker buses leave from 92–96 Nguyen Hue (District 1), roughly every 30 minutes from 9:00 am to 10:30 pm; a loop takes about an hour.
 The route passes the Zoo, the War Remnants Museum, Bui Vien, Ben Thanh Market, Nguyen Hue and the Opera House, with an audio guide.
 This is a paid tourist service and not part of the free-bus programme; check prices at the counter.
 Stay safe on the move
 Phone and bag snatching from passing motorbikes happens. Keep your phone away from the street side and bags zipped and across your body.
 Carry a light rain jacket from May to November; afternoon downpours are common.
 Offer your seat to older people, pregnant women and children.
 Questions visitors ask
 Are buses in Ho Chi Minh City free?
 Yes, for now. From 1 July to 31 December 2026 the city has waived fares on 134 city bus routes, including airport routes 109 and 152. Intercity routes and open-top sightseeing buses are not included.
 Do I need to tap a card on a free bus?
 Since 1 October 2026 every passenger has to check in when boarding, to count the trip. Nothing is charged. You can tap a Visa or Mastercard contactless card, Apple Pay, Google Pay or Samsung Pay at the reader by the door; Vietnamese residents can also use their ID card or the VNeID app. If it doesn't work, the driver or attendant will help.
 How do I get from Tan Son Nhat airport to the city centre by bus?
 Take bus 152 (via Ben Thanh Market) or bus 109 (to Saigon bus station near Ben Thanh). Both are on the free-fare list until the end of 2026. Look for the bus stop signs outside arrivals and ask airport staff if you are unsure which terminal the bus stops at.
 Can I get to the Cu Chi Tunnels by public bus?
 Yes, but it is slow. Take bus 13 from Saigon bus station to Cu Chi bus station, then bus 79 to Ben Duoc. Allow two hours or more each way. Most visitors book a tour or transfer instead.
 How much does the Saigon river bus cost?
 About 15,000 dong per trip on the Bach Dang – Linh Dong route. Boats start at 8:30 am from Bach Dang pier in District 1.
 Last checked: November 2026. Sources: free route list (Thu Vien Phap Luat) · check-in from 1 Oct (Bao Xay Dung) · free buses (Thanh Nien) · river bus and sightseeing bus (VnExpress) . Routes and rules can change; check at the stop.

# ITINERARY PLANNER
Visitors can build a 1, 2 or 3-day plan at https://hcmcinsider.com/guides/saigon-itinerary/ and a where-to-stay quiz at https://hcmcinsider.com/guides/where-to-stay-ho-chi-minh-city/#quiz.
- Old Saigon on foot (District 1 and District 3): The palace, the museum and the French-era landmarks are all within walking distance. Start early: it is cooler and the queues are short.
- Cholon: Chinatown food, temples and markets (Districts 5, 6 and 11): Saigon's Chinatown is 20–30 minutes by car from District 1 (or city bus 1). Come hungry and early: many of the best stalls are mornings only.
- Cu Chi Tunnels, then a Saigon evening (Day trip, about 70 km northwest): A half-day tour is the easy way: pickup in District 1 around 7–8 am, back in the early afternoon.
- Mekong Delta day trip (My Tho and Ben Tre): Rice fields, coconut groves and boat rides through small canals, about 2 hours each way by road.
